mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by at least 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporations and investors.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward return does not fall below the 30th percentile of similar rate hike events (p > 0.3 in t-test), or the S&P 500 20-day return is positive despite the rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index by at least 1% over two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate a disinflationary easing of policy rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 1% over two consecutive months
regime_hint: Disinflationary trend in inflation targeting regime
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to the prior month's return (p > 0.05 in paired t-test), or CPIAUCSL does not fall by ≥ 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 50,000 jobs in the following month is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by ≥ 50,000 in the next month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) compared to the prior month's 5-day return, or employment growth does not exceed 50,000 for the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly GDPC1 personal consumption expenditure turns above the prior quarter's average by at least 2%, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be positive, reflecting optimism about future economic activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds prior quarter average by ≥ 2% in the current month
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 20-day forward return is not higher than the 50th percentile of similar positive-GDPC1 events (p > 0.5 in quantile comparison).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) reading below the prior month's value by at least 2% triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as weak manufacturing output signals economic weakness and equity sell-off.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥ 2% relative to prior month
regime_hint: Structural supply shock or soft landing scare
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically worse than the prior month's (p > 0.1 in paired t-test), or INDPRO recovers by ≥ 2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both HOUST (residential construction) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 5% in the next month indicate robust demand across sectors, predicting a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥ 5% AND RSAFS increases by ≥ 5% in the following month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically superior to the average of non-interaction events (p > 0.05 in permutation test).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be positive as lower unemployment suggests a stronger labor market and equity risk tolerance.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not higher than the 40th percentile of prior low-unemployment periods (p > 0.3 in quantile comparison).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of prolonged monetary easing (defined by FEDFUNDS < 1% for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive as investors anticipate future rate cuts and increased investment.
failure_condition: Across 12 such easing months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically above the average of non-easing periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).
